title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.I: Pelagius grants supernatural grace only as law and external teaching — Aug. De grat. Christi 3; Prosper De Ingratis
pass_a_gloss: I. Pelagius therefore granted supernatural grace, but constituted in doctrine, or in the external revelation of those things which are necessary unto obtaining salvation. It is plain from Augustine, lib. 1. De gratia Christi contra Pelag. cap. 3. He places the grace of God either in nature, or in law and doctrine: so that when God helps a man, by revealing and showing what ought to be done, he is believed to help. The same may be seen in Prosper, in the Poem De Ingratis, cap. 20. Grace with you is nothing other than law, and the warning prophet, and the teaching of a minister. And in the Epistle to Ruffinus De grat. et lib. arbitr. He says they confess only this concerning grace, that it is a certain mistress unto free will, etc. But the Orthodox, by no means content with this external and admonishing grace, urged that internal grace must be acknowledged.
pass_b_english: I. Pelagius granted supernatural grace—but as doctrine, or external revelation of what is needed for salvation. Augustine makes it plain (De gratia Christi contra Pelagium 1.3): he puts God’s grace either in nature or in law and teaching, so that God is thought to help by revealing and showing what ought to be done. Prosper says the same (De Ingratis 20): With you grace is nothing but law, the warning prophet, and a minister’s teaching. And in the letter to Ruffinus on grace and free will he says they confess only that grace is somehow a mistress to free will. The Orthodox, not content with that external admonishing grace, pressed that internal grace must be acknowledged.
source_text: I. Concessit igitur Pelagius supernaturalem gratiam, sed in doctrina constitutam, sive revelatione externa earum rerum quae ad salutem consequendam sunt necessaria. Patet ex Augustino, lib. 1. De gratia Christi contra Pelag. cap. 3. Gratiam Dei aut in natura ponit, aut in lege atque doctrina: ut cum adjuvet Deus hominem, revelando et ostendendo quid fieri debeat, adjuvare credatur. Idem videre licet apud Prosperum, Carmine De Ingratis, cap. 20. Aliud non est vobiscum gratia quam lex, quamque propheta monens, et quam doctrina ministri. Et in Epistola ad Ruff. De grat. et lib. arbitr. Hoc tantum dicit eos de gratia confiteri, quod quaedam libero arbitrio sit magistra, etc. Sed Orthodoxi hac gratia externa et monitrice minime contenti, urgebant internam gratiam esse agnoscendam.
